items.name: Supreme Court of the United States
items.mission: Exercises the supreme federal judicial authority in matters within its original or appellate jurisdiction.

items.name: United States Courts of Appeals
items.mission: Thirteen courts primarily review district-court judgments and certain federal agency decisions for legal error.
items.notes: Twelve regional courts of appeals and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit; an aggregate, not a single administrative court.

items.name: United States District Courts
items.mission: Ninety-four federal trial courts resolve civil and criminal matters within their federal jurisdiction.

items.name: United States Bankruptcy Courts
items.mission: Ninety bankruptcy courts administer proceedings under federal bankruptcy law; bankruptcy courts are units of district courts.
items.notes: Count describes court units, not the 94 federal judicial districts; aggregate parented to judicial branch to avoid inaccurate one-to-one topology.

items.name: United States Court of International Trade
items.mission: Adjudicates specified customs and international trade disputes under federal law.

items.name: United States Court of Federal Claims
items.mission: Adjudicates specified monetary claims against the United States under its Article I statutory jurisdiction.
items.notes: An Article I court in the federal judicial administration, not an Article III court; organizational grouping is not a constitutional reclassification.

items.name: Administrative Office of the United States Courts
items.mission: Provides legal, financial, operational, technology, statistical and management support to the federal courts.

items.name: Federal Judicial Center
items.mission: Provides research and education to the federal judiciary and supports improved judicial administration.
items.notes: Does not make or enforce policy for the federal judiciary.

items.name: Judicial Conference of the United States
items.mission: Serves as the principal national policy-making body concerned with administration of federal courts.
